questions.title: Capsule protects against phagocytosis
questions.question: Outer covering in some bacteria that protects them from phagocytosis by host cells is?

explanations.A: Correct. The polysaccharide (or, in Bacillus anthracis, polypeptide) capsule that surrounds many bacteria is a major virulence factor precisely because it resists phagocytosis by host immune cells -- it physically masks surface molecules that phagocytes would otherwise recognise and bind. This antiphagocytic role, alongside its use in organism identification/serotyping and as a vaccine antigen (e.g. pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib vaccines), is the capsule's defining function. It is an outer covering additional to, and distinct from, the cell wall beneath it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The cell wall gives the bacterium its shape and rigidity and is a site of action for some antibiotics; protecting the cell from phagocytosis is specifically the capsule's role, not the wall's.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The flagellum is the organelle of motility, propelling the cell through liquid; it plays no role in resisting phagocytosis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Peptidoglycan is the structural mesh within the cell wall that gives it rigidity; it is not the outer antiphagocytic covering being described here.

questions.learning_objective: State that the bacterial capsule's antiphagocytic function is what protects the organism from phagocytosis, distinct from the cell wall's shape/rigidity role.
questions.source_citation: INI MCQ .pdf, Bacterial cell structure, p5

questions.title: What the bacterial cell wall does NOT do
questions.question: A bacterial cell wall does all of the following EXCEPT?

options.A: Gives shape and rigidity to the cell
options.B: Is the site of action for some antibiotics
options.C: Is associated with some symptoms of disease

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement). Peptidoglycan, the wall's structural mesh, is exactly what gives the bacterial cell its characteristic shape and rigidity.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement). Beta-lactam antibiotics (penicillins, cephalosporins) and others act by inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis, making the cell wall a genuine antibiotic target.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement). In Gram-negative bacteria the outer wall's lipopolysaccharide functions as endotoxin, directly producing disease symptoms such as fever and septic shock.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the false statement, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Protection from phagocytosis is specifically the capsule's job, not the cell wall's -- the wall instead provides shape/rigidity, is an antibiotic target, and (via its Gram-negative LPS component) contributes to disease symptoms, but resisting phagocytic engulfment is a separate, capsule-specific function.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that protection from phagocytosis is the capsule's role, not one of the cell wall's genuine functions (shape/rigidity, antibiotic target, disease symptoms via LPS).
questions.source_citation: INI MCQ .pdf, Bacterial cell structure, p5

questions.title: Flagella and pili are made of protein
questions.question: Flagella and pili are made of?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lipids are the main constituent of membranes, not of flagella or pili, which are protein appendages.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Carbohydrates are found in structures such as capsules and the outer LPS of Gram-negative walls, not as the building block of flagella or pili.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) carry genetic information; they are not structural building blocks of flagella or pili.
explanations.D: Correct. Both flagella and pili are protein appendages: the flagellum is a helical filament built from repeating subunits of the protein flagellin, rotated by a basal-body motor to drive motility, while pili are likewise protein-based surface appendages, used for adhesion (ordinary pili) or DNA transfer during conjugation (sex pili). Being built of protein, rather than lipid, carbohydrate or nucleic acid, is exactly what makes both structures antigenic and recognisable by the host immune system.

questions.learning_objective: State that both flagella and pili are protein appendages, not lipid, carbohydrate or nucleic-acid structures.
questions.source_citation: INI MCQ .pdf, Bacterial cell structure, p5

questions.title: Polysaccharide-containing structure: Gram-negative wall
questions.question: Which of the following contains polysaccharide?

explanations.A: Correct. The Gram-negative cell wall's outer membrane carries lipopolysaccharide (LPS) -- the "polysaccharide" component of the wall, attached to a lipid A anchor -- alongside its thin peptidoglycan layer and periplasmic proteins. This polysaccharide component (the LPS O-antigen) is what accounts for antigenic variation between Gram-negative strains and, as the endotoxin, drives much of the pathology in Gram-negative infection.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pili are protein appendages built from pilin subunits, not polysaccharide structures.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Flagella are protein filaments built from flagellin subunits, not polysaccharide structures.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules; they contain no polysaccharide at all.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the Gram-negative cell wall's outer LPS membrane as the polysaccharide-containing structure among the options, distinct from the protein-based pili/flagella and DNA-based plasmids.

questions.title: Bacterial pili are mainly protein
questions.question: The bacterial pili mainly contain?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Carbohydrates are found in structures such as capsules and LPS, not as the main constituent of pili.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lipids are the main constituent of membranes, not of pili, which are protein appendages.
explanations.C: Correct. Bacterial pili are protein appendages, assembled from repeating pilin subunits -- like the related flagellum (built from flagellin), a pilus is a protein filament, not a lipid, carbohydrate or mineral structure. Ordinary pili use this protein structure for adhesion to host cells or surfaces; sex pili use it for conjugative DNA transfer between bacteria.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Minerals are not a structural component of pili at all.

questions.learning_objective: State that bacterial pili are mainly protein, like the related flagellum.

questions.title: Mesosomes are part of the plasma membrane
questions.question: Mesosomes are the part of?

explanations.A: Correct. Mesosomes are invaginations (infoldings) of the bacterial cytoplasmic (plasma) membrane -- classically described as housing the respiratory-chain enzymes and increasing the membrane's surface area. Being membrane-derived, they are a prokaryotic structure with no eukaryotic counterpart and no sterol content.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The endoplasmic reticulum is a eukaryotic organelle; bacteria have no ER, and mesosomes are a distinct, membrane-derived prokaryotic structure.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lysosomes are eukaryotic digestive organelles; bacteria have no lysosomes, and mesosomes are unrelated to them structurally or functionally.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The Golgi apparatus is a eukaryotic organelle for protein sorting and packaging; bacteria have no Golgi apparatus, and mesosomes are not derived from it.

questions.learning_objective: State that mesosomes are invaginations of the bacterial plasma membrane, not any eukaryotic organelle.

questions.title: Teichoic acids in Gram-positive bacteria
questions.question: Teichoic acids are found in?

explanations.A: Correct. Teichoic acid (wall-bound) and lipoteichoic acid (membrane-anchored) are components threaded through the thick peptidoglycan wall of Gram-positive bacteria, contributing to wall charge, adhesion and immune activation. Gram-negative bacteria lack both -- they instead have an outer membrane, periplasmic space and lipopolysaccharide, none of which Gram-positive bacteria possess.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Gram-negative bacteria lack teichoic acid entirely; it is restricted to the Gram-positive wall, which has no outer membrane to compare it against.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Fungal cell walls are built from chitin and glucans, not teichoic acid, which is a bacterial (specifically Gram-positive) cell-wall component.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Teichoic acid is a genuine, well-characterised component of the Gram-positive bacterial cell wall; the correct organism group is present among the options.

questions.learning_objective: State that teichoic acid is a Gram-positive wall component, absent from Gram-negative bacteria.

questions.title: Mesosomes as sites of respiratory enzymes
questions.question: Mesosomes are?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ribosomes are separate cytoplasmic particles that carry out protein synthesis; mesosomes are membrane invaginations, structurally and functionally unrelated to ribosomes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mesosomes are a normal structural feature of the intact cell, not an artefact or product formed specifically during cell lysis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mesosomes are invaginations of the plasma membrane, not part of the cell wall, which is a separate, more external structure.
explanations.D: Correct. Mesosomes are classically described as an essential prokaryotic structure that houses cytochrome (respiratory-chain) enzymes, increasing the effective membrane surface area available for respiration -- a role broadly analogous to the mitochondrial cristae of a eukaryotic cell, though mesosomes are a bacterial (prokaryotic)-specific feature with no sterol content. This respiratory role is also why mesosomes are more prominent in Gram-positive bacteria, whose thicker wall demands a larger folded-membrane surface to sustain the same metabolic output.

questions.learning_objective: State that mesosomes house respiratory-chain enzymes, distinct from ribosomes, the cell wall, or a lysis artefact.

questions.title: Chemical composition of the bacterial capsule
questions.question: Bacterial capsule is chemically composed of?

explanations.A: Incorrect alone. Polypeptide is the capsule material in the specific case of Bacillus anthracis, but is not the general answer across bacteria as a whole -- most capsules are polysaccharide.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The capsule is not built from nucleic acid; polynucleotides are DNA/RNA, an unrelated class of molecule to capsule material.
explanations.C: Incorrect alone. Polysaccharide is the capsule material for most bacteria, but Bacillus anthracis is a well-known exception with a polypeptide capsule, so this option alone does not cover every case.
explanations.D: Correct. Most bacterial capsules are composed of polysaccharide, but Bacillus anthracis is the classic exception, with a capsule made of poly-D-glutamic acid, a polypeptide. Because the question asks for the general chemical composition of "the bacterial capsule" across organisms, the answer must cover both possibilities rather than naming only the majority case. This polysaccharide-or-polypeptide composition is also what gives the capsule its antigenic specificity, used for organism identification and vaccine preparation.

questions.learning_objective: State that most bacterial capsules are polysaccharide, with Bacillus anthracis's polypeptide capsule as the recognised exception.

questions.title: Cell wall maintains bacterial shape
questions.question: The characteristic shape of the bacteria is maintained because of?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The capsule is an outer, often gel-like layer whose role is antiphagocytic protection and antigenicity, not maintaining the cell's rigid shape.
explanations.B: Correct. Peptidoglycan (murein) -- alternating sugar chains cross-linked by short peptides -- forms a mesh-like sacculus in the cell wall that gives the bacterium its rigidity and its characteristic shape (coccus, bacillus, spirillum), and lets it resist osmotic lysis. Removing the wall (e.g. with lysozyme) produces a spherical protoplast regardless of the cell's original shape, which directly demonstrates that the wall, not any other structure, is what maintains shape.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The plasma membrane is a fluid phospholipid bilayer, not a rigid structure; it does not maintain the cell's characteristic shape on its own.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The slime layer is a loose, diffuse extracellular layer (looser than a true capsule); it is not the structure responsible for maintaining rigid cell shape.

questions.learning_objective: State that peptidoglycan in the cell wall maintains the bacterium's characteristic shape and rigidity.
questions.source_citation: INI MCQ .pdf, Bacterial cell structure, p6

questions.title: Gram+/- differences reside in the cell wall
questions.question: The differences between Gram positive and Gram-negative bacteria is shown to reside in the?

explanations.A: Correct. The cell wall is where Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria fundamentally differ: a thick peptidoglycan layer with teichoic acid (Gram-positive) versus a thin peptidoglycan layer plus an outer LPS-carrying membrane and periplasmic space (Gram-negative). This structural difference is what the Gram stain itself detects, and it underlies systematic differences in antibiotic susceptibility and toxin type (exotoxin-dominant Gram-positive vs. endotoxin-bearing Gram-negative) between the two groups.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Neither Gram-positive nor Gram-negative bacteria has a true nucleus (both are prokaryotes); the nucleus is not where the Gram-stain-relevant difference resides.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria have a similar inner cytoplasmic membrane; the defining structural difference between them is in the wall external to this membrane, not the membrane itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mesosomes are membrane invaginations found in bacteria generally; they are not the structure that distinguishes Gram-positive from Gram-negative organisms.

questions.learning_objective: State that the cell wall is where the defining structural difference between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria resides.

questions.title: Bacterial locomotion is by flagella
questions.question: Bacterial locomotion is accomplished by?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fimbriae (ordinary pili) mediate adhesion to host cells or surfaces, not locomotion -- they are not motility organelles.
explanations.B: Correct. The flagellum is specifically the organelle of motility: a helical protein filament built from flagellin, rotated by a basal-body motor to propel the cell through liquid. Fimbriae/pili, by contrast, mediate adhesion rather than movement, which is why "flagella" alone -- not "both a and b" -- is the correct answer here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bacteria lack the complex cytoskeletal motility apparatus of eukaryotic cells; locomotion is instead driven by the flagellum's own motor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Only flagella provide locomotion; fimbriae (option a) mediate adhesion, not movement, so "both" overstates fimbriae's role.

questions.learning_objective: State that flagella, not fimbriae, provide bacterial locomotion.

questions.title: Teichoic acid in Gram-positive walls
questions.question: Teichoic acid is?

options.A: Found in the walls of Gram-positive bacteria
options.C: Make up outer wall of Gram-negative bacteria
options.D: Influence the permeability of the membrane

explanations.A: Correct. Teichoic acid (wall-bound) and lipoteichoic acid (membrane-anchored) are threaded through the thick peptidoglycan wall of Gram-positive bacteria specifically -- Gram-negative bacteria lack both entirely. This location, more than any secondary property, is the defining, unambiguously true fact about teichoic acid tested here.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the best answer. Teichoic acid can serve as a bacteriophage-attachment site in some systems, but this is a secondary detail, not the defining, most reliably true statement among the options.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Teichoic acid is a Gram-positive wall component; Gram-negative bacteria's outer wall instead carries lipopolysaccharide, not teichoic acid.
explanations.D: Incorrect as the best answer. Teichoic acid contributes to wall charge and cation binding, which can have secondary effects, but this is not its defining, most directly true characteristic among the options.

questions.learning_objective: State that teichoic acid is found in the walls of Gram-positive bacteria, not the Gram-negative outer wall.

questions.title: Capsule protects and helps adherence
questions.question: What is the function of bacterial capsule?

options.B: Helps in adherence of bacteria to surface in its environment

explanations.A: Incorrect alone. Antiphagocytic protection is one genuine capsule function, but the capsule also mediates adherence, so this option alone is incomplete.
explanations.B: Incorrect alone. Adherence to surfaces is a genuine capsule function, but the capsule is also antiphagocytic, so this option alone is incomplete.
explanations.C: Correct. The bacterial capsule serves both roles at once: it resists phagocytosis by host immune cells (its major virulence-factor role, also used in organism identification/serotyping and vaccine preparation), and it helps the bacterium adhere to surfaces in its environment, contributing to colonisation and biofilm formation. Neither function alone captures the capsule's full role, which is why the composite "both a and b" is the correct answer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The capsule does have real, well-established functions (protection from phagocytosis and adherence); "none of these" is only correct if both listed functions were false, which they are not.

questions.learning_objective: State that the bacterial capsule both protects against phagocytosis and helps the organism adhere to surfaces.

questions.title: The false statement about the Gram-negative cell wall
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a gram-negative cell wall is FALSE?

options.B: It maintains the shape of the cell
options.D: It includes a thin layer of peptidoglycan

explanations.A: Correct. This is the false statement. Teichoic acid is restricted to the Gram-positive cell wall; the Gram-negative wall does not contain it, having instead an outer LPS-carrying membrane and periplasmic space that the Gram-positive wall lacks.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this is a true statement). The Gram-negative wall's thin peptidoglycan layer does still maintain the cell's characteristic shape, just as the thicker Gram-positive wall does.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this is a true statement). The lipopolysaccharide of the Gram-negative outer membrane is itself the endotoxin, directly responsible for inflammatory and septic effects when released.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this is a true statement). The Gram-negative wall's peptidoglycan layer is genuinely thin, unlike the thick Gram-positive wall.

questions.learning_objective: Identify "contains teichoic acid" as false for the Gram-negative wall, while correctly recognising its shape-maintenance, endotoxin and thin-peptidoglycan properties.

questions.title: Pilus functions: the exception
questions.question: In a prokaryotic cell all of the following are functions of the pili EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Incorrect (genuine pilus function). Sex pili specifically mediate conjugative DNA transfer between bacteria, a well-established pilus function.
explanations.B: Correct. This is the false statement, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Pili are not motility organelles -- that role belongs to the flagellum; ordinary pili mediate adhesion and sex pili mediate conjugation, but neither type propels the cell through liquid.
explanations.C: Incorrect (genuine pilus function). Pilus-mediated adhesion to surfaces and to other bacterial cells contributes to biofilm formation, a recognised pilus function.
explanations.D: Incorrect (genuine pilus function). Ordinary (common) pili are short, hair-like appendages whose main function is adhesion of the bacterium to host cells or surfaces.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that pili mediate adhesion, biofilm formation and (sex pili) DNA transfer, but never provide motility -- that is the flagellum's role.

questions.title: Only Gram-negative cells have an LPS layer
questions.question: Which of the following is a difference between gram-positive and gram-negative cells?

options.A: Only gram-negative cells have a lipopolysaccharide (LPS) layer
options.B: Only gram-positive cells have peptidoglycan that is made of a carbohydrate backbone
options.C: Gram-negative cell walls contain teichoic acids
options.D: Gram-positive cells contain less peptidoglycan than do gram-negative cells

explanations.A: Correct. LPS is carried on the outer membrane that is unique to the Gram-negative cell envelope; Gram-positive bacteria have no outer membrane and so no LPS layer at all. This is a genuine, unambiguous structural difference between the two groups, unlike the other three options, each of which misstates a real fact.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Both Gram-positive and Gram-negative peptidoglycan share the same alternating-sugar (carbohydrate) backbone structure, cross-linked by peptides; this is not a distinguishing feature between the two groups.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Teichoic acid is restricted to the Gram-positive wall; Gram-negative cell walls do not contain it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The relationship is reversed: Gram-positive cells have a thick peptidoglycan wall, containing more peptidoglycan than the thin Gram-negative wall.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that only Gram-negative cells have an LPS outer-membrane layer, and reject the false peptidoglycan-backbone, teichoic-acid and relative-thickness distractors.

questions.title: Endotoxin is present in lipopolysaccharide
questions.question: Endotoxin produced by gram negative bacteria is present in?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Peptidoglycan gives the wall its rigidity; it is not itself the endotoxin.
explanations.B: Correct. Endotoxin is not a secreted product but a structural part of the Gram-negative outer membrane -- specifically the lipopolysaccharide (LPS), whose lipid A component is what triggers the inflammatory and septic effects released mainly when the bacterium lyses. This structural, non-secreted nature is exactly what distinguishes endotoxin from the actively secreted protein exotoxins.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Teichoic acid is a Gram-positive wall component; Gram-negative bacteria (the organisms that produce endotoxin) do not have it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inner (cytoplasmic) membrane is a standard bacterial structure shared with Gram-positive organisms; LPS/endotoxin is specifically on the outer membrane, not the inner one.

questions.learning_objective: State that endotoxin is the lipopolysaccharide of the Gram-negative outer membrane, not peptidoglycan, teichoic acid or the inner membrane.

questions.title: Exotoxins are heat labile
questions.question: Exotoxins are?

explanations.A: Correct. Exotoxins are secreted proteins/polypeptides, and being proteins, their three-dimensional structure -- and therefore their toxic activity -- is destroyed by heat (heat labile). This is the opposite of endotoxin, which is a heat-stable (thermostable) lipopolysaccharide that survives heating that would inactivate an exotoxin.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Heat stability is a property of endotoxin (lipopolysaccharide), not of exotoxins, which are heat-labile proteins.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Exotoxins are actively secreted by the living bacterium, not a structural part of the cell wall -- that description instead fits endotoxin (LPS).
explanations.D: Incorrect. Exotoxins are individual secreted polypeptide/protein toxins, not generically described as "polymerized complexes."

questions.learning_objective: State that exotoxins are heat labile (being proteins), the opposite of heat-stable endotoxin.

questions.title: Flagella are the organ of motility
questions.question: Flagella?

options.B: Can be seen by gram stain
options.D: Play a role in bacterial adherence

explanations.A: Incorrect as the defining statement. Some coccal species can be flagellated, but flagella are not a general or defining feature of cocci as a shape category; this is not the correctly generalisable statement about flagella.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Flagella are too thin to be resolved by ordinary Gram staining and light microscopy; visualising them requires a special flagellar stain or electron microscopy.
explanations.C: Correct. The flagellum's defining role is motility: a helical protein filament built from flagellin, rotated by a basal-body motor to propel the bacterium through liquid. This is the general, always-true statement about flagella, unlike the organism-specific or technique-specific claims in the other options.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Adherence is specifically the role of pili/fimbriae, not flagella, whose role is motility.

questions.learning_objective: State that flagella are the bacterial organ of motility, distinct from pili's adherence role.

questions.title: Exotoxin characters: the exception
questions.question: One of the following is NOT a character of exotoxins?

options.D: Prepared by disintegration of the organism

explanations.A: Incorrect (genuine exotoxin character). Exotoxins are actively secreted, diffusing out of the living bacterial cell into the surrounding environment.
explanations.B: Incorrect (genuine exotoxin character). Exotoxins typically act on a specific target (e.g. a specific receptor or tissue), unlike the broad, nonspecific effects of endotoxin.
explanations.C: Incorrect (genuine exotoxin character). As proteins, exotoxins are strongly antigenic, which is exactly what allows them to be converted into immunogenic toxoids for vaccines.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the false statement, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Exotoxins are actively secreted by the living, intact bacterium -- they are not released only when the organism disintegrates. Release upon bacterial disintegration/lysis is instead the release mechanism of endotoxin (LPS), which is a structural component of the cell rather than a secreted product.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that exotoxins are actively secreted, not released only by bacterial disintegration -- that release mechanism belongs to endotoxin instead.

questions.title: Endotoxin characters: the exception
questions.question: One of the following is NOT a character of endotoxins?

options.C: Changed into formol toxoid if incubated with 0.3% formalin

explanations.A: Incorrect (genuine endotoxin character). Being a lipopolysaccharide rather than a protein, endotoxin is heat stable (thermostable), surviving heating that would destroy a protein exotoxin.

questions.title: The correct statement about exotoxin
questions.question: Which statement is correct for bacteria exotoxin?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Exotoxins are actively secreted and diffuse out of the bacterial cell; "non-diffusible/cell-bound" instead describes the structural, non-secreted nature of endotoxin.
explanations.B: Correct. Exotoxins are proteins, and as proteins they are strongly antigenic -- the host mounts a specific antibody response against them, and this same antigenicity is exploited to produce toxoid vaccines by formalin-inactivating the toxin while preserving its immunogenicity. This is the opposite of endotoxin, which as a lipopolysaccharide is only weakly antigenic.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Exotoxins typically act with high specificity on a particular target or tissue; nonspecific action instead describes endotoxin's broad inflammatory effects.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lipopolysaccharide is the chemical nature of endotoxin, not exotoxin, which is a secreted protein/polypeptide.

questions.learning_objective: State that exotoxins are strongly antigenic proteins, distinct from endotoxin's non-diffusible, nonspecific, lipopolysaccharide nature.

questions.title: Endotoxin association is due to lipopolysaccharide
questions.question: The association of endotoxin in G–ve bacteria is a result of presence of?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Peptidoglycan provides rigidity to the cell wall; it is not itself the endotoxin.
explanations.B: Correct. Endotoxin activity in Gram-negative bacteria is a direct result of the lipopolysaccharide (LPS) that forms part of their outer membrane -- specifically the lipid A portion of LPS is what triggers the toxic, inflammatory effects. This structural association is why endotoxin is unique to Gram-negative organisms, which alone possess an LPS-carrying outer membrane.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Polypeptide is not the chemical basis of endotoxin; endotoxin is specifically lipopolysaccharide, a lipid-carbohydrate complex.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Steroids play no role in bacterial endotoxin; endotoxin activity is due to lipopolysaccharide.
explanations.E: Incorrect. "Calcified proteins" is not a recognised bacterial structure and plays no role in endotoxin activity, which is due to lipopolysaccharide.

questions.title: The character that best matches exotoxins
questions.question: Which one of the following characters is best matching with bacterial exotoxins?

options.B: They are not affected by formalin
options.C: They are produced only when the organism disintegrates

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lipopolysaccharide is the chemical nature of endotoxin, not exotoxin, which is a secreted protein/polypeptide.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Exotoxins are affected by formalin -- formalin treatment converts an exotoxin into an inactivated but still-immunogenic toxoid, the basis of toxoid vaccines.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Release upon organism disintegration describes endotoxin (a structural component); exotoxins are instead actively secreted by the living, intact bacterium.
explanations.D: Correct. Exotoxins are among the most potent biological toxins known -- some are lethal in microgram quantities (e.g. botulinum and tetanus toxin) -- which is why "they are strong" is the best-matching general character among the options. This extreme potency, together with their protein nature, antigenicity and heat lability, distinguishes exotoxins from the comparatively weaker, broad-acting endotoxin.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Thermostability (heat stability) is a property of endotoxin; exotoxins are heat labile, since they are proteins whose structure is destroyed by heat.

questions.learning_objective: Identify potency ("they are strong") as the character best matching exotoxins, rejecting properties that instead belong to endotoxin.

questions.title: Pili occur in both motile and non-motile strains
questions.question: Bacterial pili is characterized by one of the following?

options.A: It's formed mainly by gram positive bacteria
options.B: Occur in motile & non motile strains

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pili are a well-characterised feature of many Gram-negative bacteria (e.g. E. coli fimbriae, sex pili in conjugation); they are not a feature formed mainly by Gram-positive organisms.
explanations.B: Correct. Because pili are used for adhesion (and, for sex pili, DNA transfer) rather than motility, their presence is independent of whether a strain is motile -- pili can be found on both motile and non-motile bacterial strains alike. This independence from motility is exactly what distinguishes a pilus from a flagellum, which by definition requires the cell to be motile.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pili are generally shorter and thinner than flagella, not longer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pili, being protein structures, are antigenic -- the host immune system can raise antibodies against pilin subunits.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Formation under unfavourable/nutrient-limited conditions describes bacterial endospore formation, not pilus formation, which is a constitutive or regulated surface-appendage feature unrelated to sporulation triggers.

questions.learning_objective: State that pili occur independently of motility (in both motile and non-motile strains), and reject the false Gram-positive, length, antigenicity and sporulation-trigger distractors.

questions.title: Lipopolysaccharide is responsible for endotoxin activity
questions.question: Which is responsible for endotoxin activity in Gram negative bacteria?

explanations.A: Correct. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), specifically its lipid A component, is the molecule directly responsible for endotoxin activity -- the fever, inflammation and septic-shock effects seen with Gram-negative infection -- and it is a structural part of the Gram-negative outer membrane rather than a secreted product. This is also why endotoxin activity is unique to Gram-negative organisms -- Gram-positive bacteria have no outer membrane and so carry no LPS at all.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lipoprotein (such as Braun's lipoprotein) anchors the outer membrane to the peptidoglycan layer structurally; it is not the molecule responsible for endotoxin activity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Outer membrane proteins serve transport and structural roles; endotoxin activity is specifically attributable to LPS, not to the membrane's protein components.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The periplasmic space is a compartment holding transport and hydrolytic proteins between the two Gram-negative membranes; it is not itself the molecule responsible for endotoxin activity.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Teichoic acid is a Gram-positive wall component, absent from Gram-negative bacteria altogether, and plays no role in endotoxin activity.

questions.learning_objective: State that lipopolysaccharide is responsible for endotoxin activity in Gram-negative bacteria.

questions.title: Exotoxin properties: the exception
questions.question: All are true about exotoxins EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Correct. This is the false statement, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Many exotoxin genes are carried on plasmids or lysogenic bacteriophages rather than exclusively on the bacterial chromosome (e.g. diphtheria toxin is phage-encoded, and several enterotoxins are plasmid-encoded), so "coded by chromosome" is not a universal exotoxin property.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement). Exotoxins are, by definition, secreted polypeptide/protein toxins.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement). Being proteins, exotoxins are heat labile -- their toxic activity is destroyed by heat, unlike heat-stable endotoxin.
explanations.D: Incorrect (true statement). Exotoxins typically show specific action, targeting a particular tissue, cell type or receptor, unlike the broad, nonspecific effects of endotoxin.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that exotoxin genes are not exclusively chromosome-coded (many are plasmid- or phage-encoded), while correctly recognising their protein nature, heat lability and specific action.
